title: Microsoft 365 Copilot connectors: custom icons and display names for custom connectors
summary: The briefing passes: the rename endpoint, delegated administrator requirement, licensing and inventory route are supported. One minor documentation discrepancy remains: another Microsoft Graph guide refers to a search admin managing connections, whereas the cited connector-management page requires an AI administrator.

claims.claim: Delegated ExternalConnection.ReadWrite.OwnedBy requires the signed-in user to be an administrator.
claims.quote: Allows the app to read and write settings of external connections on behalf of a signed-in user. The signed-in user must be an administrator.

claims.claim: Delegated ExternalConnection.ReadWrite.All requires the signed-in user to be an administrator.
claims.quote: Allows the app to read and write all external connections on behalf of a signed-in user. The signed-in user must be an administrator.

claims.claim: Apps with the update permission can modify connections within that permission's authorization scope.
claims.quote: The app can only read and write external connections that it is authorized to, or it can create new external connections.

claims.claim: The cited connector-management page requires the AI administrator role to access and manage connectors in the admin center.
claims.quote: To access and manage your Microsoft 365 Copilot connectors, you must be an AI administrator for your organization.
claims.fix: Keep the AI administrator requirement. Add: 'The Microsoft Graph connection-management guide instead says a search admin can view and manage all connections in the tenant.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/graph/connecting-external-content-manage-connections, which states: 'A search admin can view and manage all the connections in the tenant'.
